citations.authors: Glaws KR, Juneau CM, Becker LC, Di Stasi SL, Hewett TE
citations.title: Intra- and inter-rater reliability of the selective functional movement assessment (SFMA)
citations.journal: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
citations.what_it_says: First psychometric study: reliability varied from poor to good by movement pattern, with greater SFMA experience associated with better agreement.

citations.authors: Dolbeer J, Mason J, Morris J, Crowell M, Goss D
citations.title: Inter-rater reliability of the Selective Functional Movement Assessment (SFMA) by SFMA certified physical therapists with similar clinical and rating experience
citations.journal: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
citations.what_it_says: In 49 patients with pain, experienced certified PTs achieved moderate-or-better agreement on 10 of 15 movements; composite ICC 0.72 real-time.

citations.authors: Stanek JM, Smith J, Petrie J
citations.title: Intra- and inter-rater reliability of the Selective Functional Movement Assessment (SFMA) in healthy participants
citations.journal: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
citations.what_it_says: Certified clinicians with greater SFMA experience demonstrated adequate reliability with the categorical scoring method; cervical patterns weakest.

citations.authors: Harper B, Aron A
citations.title: Novice Inter-Rater Reliability on the Selective Functional Movement Assessment (SFMA) After a 4-Hour Training Session
citations.journal: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
citations.what_it_says: DPT students achieved moderate inter-rater reliability after 4 hours of training but identified fewer dysfunctions than a certified clinician.

citations.authors: Aghi A, Salvagnini D, Berton G, et al.
citations.title: Selective Functional Movement Assessment (SFMA) Reliability and Proposal of Its Use in Sports
citations.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
citations.what_it_says: In 28 competitive athletes, inter-rater reliability between expert and briefly-trained student was good (Kappa 0.60-0.62); intra-rater only moderate.

citations.authors: Riebel M, Crowell M, Dolbeer J, Szymanek E, Goss D
citations.title: Correlation of self-reported outcome measures and the Selective Functional Movement Assessment (SFMA): an exploration of validity
citations.journal: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
citations.what_it_says: In 85 patients re-tested after 6 weeks, improvements in self-reported function correlated with reductions in painful SFMA patterns but NOT consistently with movement-quality changes; mixed construct validity.

citations.authors: Huang L, Liu H, Zhao L, Peng L
citations.title: The Effect of Exercise Intervention Based Upon the Selective Functional Movement Assessment in an Athlete With Non-specific Low Back Pain: A Case Report and Pilot Study
citations.what_it_says: 8-week SFMA-guided program in one athlete with chronic low back pain reduced pain and disability; low-level (n=1) evidence of clinical utility.

citations.authors: Goshtigian GR, Swanson BT
citations.title: Using the Selective Functional Movement Assessment and regional interdependence theory to guide treatment of an athlete with back pain: a case report
citations.journal: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
citations.what_it_says: Case report demonstrating SFMA breakouts directing treatment to remote impairments with positive outcomes; illustrative, lowest-tier evidence.

citations.authors: Cook G, Burton L, Hoogenboom BJ, Voight M
citations.title: Functional movement screening: the use of fundamental movements as an assessment of function - part 1
citations.journal: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
citations.what_it_says: Foundational paper by the system's creators describing the FMS/SFMA conceptual framework and rationale underlying the certification.

citations.authors: Moran RW, Schneiders AG, Mason J, Sullivan SJ
citations.title: Do Functional Movement Screen (FMS) composite scores predict subsequent injury? A systematic review with meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: CRITICAL: only a small association between FMS composite scores and injury; methodological limitations mean FMS composites should not be relied on for injury prognosis.

citations.authors: Bonazza NA, Smuin D, Onks CA, Silvis ML, Dhawan A
citations.title: Reliability, Validity, and Injury Predictive Value of the Functional Movement Screen: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Excellent inter-rater reliability and increased injury odds with scores ≤14, but heterogeneity limits use as a standalone injury-prediction tool.

citations.authors: Dorrel BS, Long T, Shaffer S, Myer GD
citations.title: Evaluation of the Functional Movement Screen as an Injury Prediction Tool Among Active Adult Populations: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: CRITICAL: high specificity (85.7%) but very low sensitivity (24.7%); findings do not support the predictive validity of the FMS.

citations.authors: Whittaker JL, Booysen N, de la Motte S, et al.
citations.title: Predicting sport and occupational lower extremity injury risk through movement quality screening: a systematic review
citations.what_it_says: CRITICAL: evidence that poor movement quality is associated with increased injury risk was inconsistent across 17 mostly low-quality studies.

citations.authors: Bahr R
citations.title: Why screening tests to predict injury do not work—and probably never will…: a critical review
citations.what_it_says: CRITICAL: influential conceptual critique demonstrating no screening test has met the validation steps required to predict and prevent sports injuries.
